text: Erin is now completely off gluten. Her doctor confirmed coeliac last month, so no more bringing her those almond croissants.
Tariq's daughter Zara has her first swimming gala on Saturday. He's more nervous than she is, apparently.
Remind me to ask Manon how her mum's knee operation went on Tuesday.

Victor supports Fulham and has had a season ticket for twenty years. He goes with his son every home game and they have the same pie and Bovril at half time, without fail. Do not mention the Brentford game. He's also really into fly fishing, goes up to the Tweed every September with his brother-in-law Graham, and ties all his own flies.
Felix and his wife are celebrating their tenth anniversary on June 3rd. They're thinking of going back to Lisbon, where they got engaged.
Picked up the dry cleaning and booked the car in for its MOT next Thursday. Still need to sort the gutters before November.
Mabel has started knitting jumpers for her grandson Louis. She's on her third one and he's only eight months old.
Paolo doesn't drink at all, so get alcohol-free prosecco for the party on Friday.
Chiara mentioned her brother Theo is moving to Edinburgh in a fortnight for a new job at the university. She's going to miss him a lot.
Julia is reading her way through every Agatha Christie in publication order. She's up to 1934.

Long chat with Joe after football. His dad has been in hospital since Sunday with pneumonia and Joe has been driving up to Leicester every evening after work. He sounded exhausted and said his sister Giulia is flying back from Milan on 11/2 to take over for a week. I should drop round some food for him this weekend, maybe that lamb curry he likes, and text him on Monday to see how his dad is doing.
Abigail's son Noah got into the county cricket squad! First training session is next Tuesday.
Kemal is vegan but eats honey, which I did not know. Also hates mushrooms with a passion.
Don't forget to send Sinead the recipe for the lemon drizzle she liked.

Bethany's birthday is May 14. She's been dropping hints about a new set of watercolour brushes, the sable ones, because she's started painting seriously again since her daughter left for uni. She does landscapes mostly, and she's joined a class on Wednesday nights at the community centre. Her husband apparently got her a slow cooker last year and she has not forgiven him.
Dev and Sunil are doing the London to Brighton bike ride on Sunday. Dev's been training since April; Sunil has done about two rides.
Rahul told me the trip to Kyoto with his parents is off because his mum broke her wrist. They might try again in the spring.
Tomás plays bass in a covers band called The Late Shift. Their next gig is at the Crown on 12/6.
Kaito has a peanut allergy, the serious kind with an EpiPen. Remember this when we do the team lunch.
Heather's husband Graham retires on Friday after thirty-two years at the council. She's organising a surprise dinner at the Italian place on Saturday night and I'm bringing the cake.
Need to call Eamon tomorrow and wish him luck for his driving test on Thursday. Third attempt and he is a bag of nerves about it.
Olivia's sister had her baby on Monday, a little girl called Mabel. Olivia is officially an auntie and won't stop showing photos.
Dalia is obsessed with sourdough at the moment. Her starter is called Doughvid and she feeds it twice a day.
Joseph and his partner just adopted a rescue greyhound called Biscuit. He's very shy and sleeps about twenty hours a day.
Must buy a card for Uncle Victor's seventieth. The party is the 22nd, so it needs to be posted by Wednesday at the latest.
Caught up with Erin at the market. Her partner is training for the Chicago marathon on October 11th, and she's basically become a marathon widow. She said he only eats plain pasta and bananas now.
Tariq loves Arsenal, single malt whisky and terrible puns. Good to know for Christmas.
Manon's wedding in Brittany was cancelled. She and Louis split up in August. I should invite her round for dinner one evening next week.
Grocery list for Saturday: oat milk, chickpeas, coriander, two lemons. Meal prep Sunday afternoon.
Felix said his mum has started chemo and the first round went better than expected. Next one is in three weeks. He's holding up, but only just.
Paolo's kids are both mad about Pokémon cards. Noah, the older one, wants the Charizard booster box for his birthday on 3/9.
Remind me to ask Chiara how Theo's first week in Edinburgh went.
Julia has a big presentation to the board on Thursday and she's terrified. I said I'd text her that morning. Also, she only drinks oat flat whites now, so get that if I'm grabbing coffee before.
Joe Wright from the allotment grows chillies, about fourteen varieties. He gave me a jar of his scotch bonnet jam.
Giulia doesn't eat pork or shellfish. Keep that in mind for the barbecue next Saturday.
Abigail and her husband are expecting their second in February. She has had awful morning sickness, so maybe drop off some ginger biscuits.
I'm hosting book club on Wednesday. We're doing The Remains of the Day.
Kemal's grandad passed away last week. The funeral is Friday in Bursa and Kemal flies out tomorrow. I need to message him before he goes.
Sinead just got a place on the master's in archaeology at Galway, starting in September. She's thrilled. Send her congratulations, and maybe a book on Irish hill forts as a present.
Theo collects vintage Lego, mostly the space sets from the eighties. His holy grail is the Galaxy Explorer.
Bethany's little boy, Felix, starts reception next Monday. She is more anxious about it than he is, and has already bought three lunchboxes.

Phone call with Dev's mum this evening. Dev has been offered a promotion to head of engineering, starting May 1st, but he hasn't decided whether to take it because it means moving to Manchester. His girlfriend Olivia isn't keen. Must remember to call Dev before the weekend, and don't bring it up at Sunil's birthday drinks on Saturday.

Rahul is the only person I know who genuinely likes durian. He also makes the best dal I have ever eaten, which he says is his nan's recipe and he won't share it. He's a huge chess nerd too, plays online every night and is about 1900 rated. His brother Sunil is apparently even better but refuses to play him anymore after some argument at Diwali.
Tomás and Heather are having a joint housewarming on the 15th. Their cat, Pepper, will apparently be hiding under the bed the whole time.

Kaito Sato is doing the Tokyo marathon on 3/1. He wants to get under four hours this time, after missing it by two minutes last year. He's doing long runs every Sunday and has cut out beer completely until race day, which for Kaito is a huge sacrifice. His wife and both kids are going over with him and they'll stay on for a week afterwards to see her parents in Osaka. I should ask him next month how the training's going.
Graham's knee is playing up again, so he's had to stop playing walking football. He's quite down about it. Check in with him on Friday.
Eamon passed his test! Fourth time lucky in the end. I should take him out for a pint to celebrate.

Long call with Olivia Reyes. Her dad, Dr Reyes, is finally retiring on June 30th, and the family are throwing him a party at the golf club that weekend. Her brother Joseph is flying in from Toronto on the 27th and staying for a fortnight. Olivia wants everyone to chip in for a set of new irons, so remind me to send her forty quid by Friday.
Dalia hates coriander. It tastes like soap to her, she says. Learnt this the hard way tonight.
Mabel's dog Rolo had his operation yesterday. He's recovering, but she's been up all night with him. Remind me to text her tomorrow evening.
